I farm only 6 mu, but I have done this for 30 years, so I will keep the wheat-maize rotation on all 6 mu and aim for steady output rather than taking risks. Because I have well irrigation, I will manage for reliable yields and not depend only on rain. For wheat, I will use improved seed because I want stable emergence, lodging resistance, and a crop I know how to manage well. I will put most of the fertilizer into wheat and irrigate several times because, on my land, wheat responds well when water and nitrogen are not short. For summer maize, I will plant hybrid seed because that is what I would trust for stronger yield on a small area. I will still fertilize maize well, but a bit less than wheat in phosphorus and with fewer irrigations because the summer season usually has more rainfall. I will use rotary tillage because it is practical on a small farm and fits my usual way of preparing land between wheat and maize. I will keep pesticide use moderate, only enough to protect the crop and avoid obvious losses, because I want the work to stay manageable for my household.
